title: Form is emptiness
hookLine: form is emptiness, emptiness is form: nothing stands on its own

lines: WHERE DID THE CUP COME FROM?
A KNOT OF A THOUSAND THREADS.
cards: Pick up the nearest cup. Where did it come from? A store, fine.

Before that, a factory, or a potter's wheel. Before that, clay dug from a riverbank, water, a kiln's fire, fuel for the fire, the trucks, the roads, the people who made the roads, and the breakfasts that fed them.
Follow the threads long enough and the cup looks less like one solid thing and more like a knot where a thousand threads cross. That's a way in to the line the Heart Sutra is known for.

teach.h: FORM IS EMPTINESS, EMPTINESS IS FORM.
teach.b: Right after Avalokiteshvara sees the five heaps empty, the sutra turns to the monk Shariputra and says the line people chant across Asia: form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.
Emptiness is not different from form, and form is not different from emptiness. Then the same is said for feeling, perception, formations and consciousness.

teach.h: SHUNYA: EMPTY, THE SAME WORD AS ZERO.
teach.b: Today's word, shunyata, comes from shunya, empty. Sanskrit also uses shunya for zero.
But in Mahayana teaching, empty means empty of something: svabhava, own-being, an existence that stands on its own, from its own side, depending on nothing else.
So form is emptiness means the cup, the body, any form at all, has no being that stands alone. It's made entirely of other things, causes and conditions, clay and fire and hands.
And emptiness is form means this emptiness isn't off in some other realm. It's right here as the cup. It's what the cup is like.
You might hear an echo. In the Pali texts you've been reading, the Buddha taught dependent arising: everything comes to be because of other things.
Mahayana teachers, and especially the Indian philosopher Nagarjuna, drew that thread all the way out.
If everything depends on other things, nothing has a self of its own. That's emptiness. It isn't meant to be gloomy.
Some teachers turn it the other way round: nothing stands alone, so nothing is truly alone.

how: Mahayana Buddhists chant 'form is emptiness, emptiness is form' daily as part of the Heart Sutra, and many teachers explain emptiness through dependent arising: nothing exists on its own, apart from causes and conditions.

o: empty of standing alone; made of other things
a quiet mind cleared of every thought
a void where nothing really exists at all

games.q: match each piece of today's teaching.
p: empty; also the word for zero
the monk the sutra speaks to
drew dependent arising all the way out

s: it means things are empty of standing alone; the cup is still a cup.
shunya is the same Sanskrit word used for zero
Indian mathematicians used it for the number zero.
the sutra applies emptiness to all five heaps, not just form
the same is said of feeling, perception, formations and consciousness.

games.q: you're Shariputra, and you've just heard 'form is emptiness.' what comes right after?
o: 'and emptiness is form: not different from each other.'
games.why: the sutra balances it at once: emptiness is form. emptiness isn't somewhere else; it's how form is.

practice: Hold a cup, or picture one, and follow three or four of its threads as far as they go: the material, the maker, the fire, the water, the hands that carried it, the sun that grew the food for those hands. Then look at the cup again.
It's still a cup, and it's also a meeting place of countless things; let both be true at once.

wordCard.voice: Shunyata. Emptiness: not nothing, but empty of standing alone. Form is emptiness, emptiness is form.

orig.note: Sanskrit śūnyatā: emptiness, from śūnya, empty, which also means zero.

carryVoice: Your line: nothing stands alone. Not the cup, not your own body. See you tomorrow.
